summary: Assign each expression morph channel to animation, procedural behavior or direct interaction at a given time, then combine only through declared envelopes and reset rules.
objective: Facial and expressive shape-key playback remains stable when clips, gaze/blink logic and user controls overlap, without stale or silently overwritten weights.
applies_when: Blender relative shape keys are exported as glTF morph targets for facial or expressive animation.
Animation clips and procedural controls may both write morph weights.
intent_signals: blend facial morph clips with procedural blinking
prevent animation mixer from overwriting morph slider
reset shape key weights between actions
example_prompts: Play a smile clip while a procedural blink owns eyelid channels.
Expose an expression slider that temporarily takes ownership from clip animation.
negative_signals: Writing a morphTargetInfluences entry directly while an active track writes the same property with no arbitration.
Treating expression weights as physical muscle force or collision deformation.

principles: Use a channel ownership table: for each named expression, declare whether a clip, procedural system, interaction, or composed envelope writes its weight in each state. First inspect the actual loaded track binding: a glTF weight channel may bind the complete morphTargetInfluences vector rather than one independently owned named entry.

Blender relative shape keys and glTF morph targets are delta-based, but this profile focuses on playback weights and ownership. Validate full vertex/attribute correspondence with the dedicated topology-compatibility profile.

Order composition deliberately. Examples include animation base plus bounded blink offset, mutually exclusive viseme selection, or an interaction override that releases back to the current evaluated clip weight.
implementation: In Blender, preserve stable Basis-relative shape-key names, preview combinations, key intended values, and enable both shape-key data and shape-key animation export. Reset unkeyed shape keys between exported actions when clips must start neutral.

In Three.js, resolve names through each Mesh.morphTargetDictionary and route writes through one channel arbiter. Inspect imported morph-track bindings: when a clip owns the whole morphTargetInfluences vector, either construct validated indexed tracks for independently owned entries or evaluate the clip into a base vector and apply one explicit post-mixer vector composer every update. A direct single-index write made before mixer.update is not protected from a later whole-vector animation write.

Capture default weights after load. On stop, interrupt, model swap or reset, restore declared defaults and clear procedural envelopes; report missing names or differing primitive dictionaries instead of shifting indices silently.
observable_checks: Neutral, single-expression and combined-expression fixtures match the declared channel table, with no stale smile or blink after stop/reset.

While a direct slider owns one channel, an active whole-vector glTF morph track changes other expressions but cannot overwrite that channel after mixer evaluation; release returns to the current evaluated base without a discontinuity under the chosen indexed-track or post-mixer composition policy.
Every declared expression name resolves to the intended influence index on each relevant mesh, and topology compatibility is linked to its separate validation result.

creative_affordances: Expressions may be realistic, graphic, creature-like, mechanical, symbolic or deliberately impossible.
Procedural envelopes may encode blinks, breathing, speech accents, damage or audience interaction.
known_limits: Morph weights are controls over rendered deltas, not a biomechanical or physical guarantee.
The cited Mesh docs call `[0,1]` typical, not universal; this record requires a project-owned range/clamp policy.
No shape-key export or morph playback was run.

claims.statement: Blender relative shape keys define each shape relative to the Basis or another key and combine their weighted differences additively.

source_refs.locator: Relative or Absolute Shape Keys; Basis

claims.statement: glTF morph targets contain attribute deltas and animation may target morph weights; all primitives of a mesh use the same target count and order.
claims.scope: glTF 2.0.1 transport facts; detailed attribute validation belongs to the related topology profile.

claims.statement: Three.js Mesh exposes a morph target name-to-index dictionary and influence array when morph targets are detected.
claims.scope: Live Three.js Mesh API; project range and ownership policies are authored guidance.
